title: Self-similar Organization of Information in Language
abstract: arXiv:2611.26935v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: How much information relevant to predicting the future of a passage (i.e. predictive information) is carried by the preceding text, and how is this information distributed along that history? These questions are fundamental to understanding both the statistical structure of language and what large language models (LLMs) can learn about it. Indeed, LLMs trained to predict the next token in text must exploit this predictive information, so its organization determines how the structure of language becomes available to the model to learn. We develop a theory for the organization of predictive information based on the scaling behavior of a family of information measures, and the theory predicts that if this organization has the same form at all measured length scales -- i.e., it has a self-similar structure -- then the information measures evaluated at different lengths collapse onto a common form. translated_title: 语言中信息的自相似组织
translated_abstract: 与前文文本相关的、用于预测后续内容的信息量（即预测信息）有多少，以及这些信息如何沿着文本历史分布？这些问题对于理解语言的统计结构以及大语言模型（LLMs）能够从中学到什么都至关重要。事实上，训练用于预测文本中下一个词元的LLM必须利用这种预测信息，因此其组织方式决定了语言结构如何变得可供模型学习。我们基于一系列信息度量的标度行为，发展了一种关于预测信息组织的理论，该理论预测：如果这种组织在所有测量长度尺度上具有相同的形式——即具有自相似结构——那么在不同长度上评估的信息度量将坍缩到一个共同的形式。我们在长文本中观察到了这种标度坍缩现象。
tldr: 本文提出了一种基于信息度量标度行为的预测信息组织理论，并通过在长文本中观察到不同长度尺度上信息度量的标度坍缩，证明了语言中预测信息具有自相似结构，这对理解语言的统计规律及大语言模型如何学习语言结构具有重要意义。
